reasons: The dip would mean an object 32.8 times the size of Jupiter, too big to be a planet (limit 2.5).

eb.plain_summary: Not a planet, but still interesting: this is a pair of close stars eclipsing each other every 9.3 days.
key_facts: Time for the two stars to go once around each other.
Detached: well apart. Semi-detached: one star fills its space and may pass gas to the other. Contact: the stars touch. Judged from the light-curve shape.
Light lost when the brighter star is hidden.
Light lost when the fainter star is hidden.
0.5 means exactly halfway between main eclipses, as for a circular orbit.
How long the main / second eclipse lasts.
Fainter star's temperature divided by the brighter star's, from the eclipse depths. Rough: assumes similar eclipse shapes.
e cos w, e sin w (approx.)
Rough hints of an oval (eccentric) orbit from the second eclipse's position and width. Both near 0 means a circular orbit.
in the TESS eclipsing binary catalog: period 9.3911 days, type semi-detached
